record.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
record.scope: IGGLYBUFF (1 star), JIGGLYPUFF (2 stars) and WIGGLYTUFF (3 stars) declare ABILITY SING with maxPP 100 and range 2; none declares a passive. IGGLYBUFF is NORMAL/FAIRY/BABY, the other two NORMAL/FAIRY/SOUND.
record.summary: Board-wide sleep on a limited number of enemies. The caster puts every enemy on the board into a ranking, sorts it by positionY (ascending when the enemy team is BLUE, descending otherwise) and calls triggerSleep on the first N of that ranking, where N is 1/2/3 (5 fallback) by caster stars. The requested sleep duration is round(2000 ms (4000 for the fallback star) x (1 + AP/100) x critPower-if-crit). No damage is dealt. Each sleep is refused or modified by the target's own state (see effects). The cast target is not used (requiresTarget false).

targeting.who: the first N enemies of the whole board after sorting by positionY, N = 1/2/3 by caster stars (5 fallback); no range limit
targeting.note: requiresTarget false: the cast does not need a target in reach. The comparator reads only a.team (an enemy team), so every enemy in the list is ordered by the same rule: enemies of the BLUE team ascending positionY, enemies of the RED team descending positionY. Which row is 'front' in practice depends on board orientation and was not traced; no claim is made about nearest or farthest.

geometry.detail: Board.forEach collects every enemy; the first N after the positionY sort receive the status. Ties in positionY keep the order produced by Array.sort over a row-major collection (stable sort), i.e. lower x first within a row, not verified at runtime.

effects.target: the first N enemies of the sorted ranking

declaredRaw.formula: triggerSleep(round(base x (1 + AP/100) x (crit ? critPower : 1)), target)

effects.scaling: REQUESTED duration: 2000 ms for 1-, 2- and 3-star casters (4000 ms fallback), times 1 + AP/100, times the caster's critPower if the cast crit. Targets: 1 / 2 / 3 enemies for 1 / 2 / 3 stars. APPLIED duration in triggerSleep: x1.3 under NIGHT weather, x0.7 under ZENITH, halved when the target is enraged, then applyStatusDurationReductions (Swift Swim x0.7, else Hydration x0.5, else Water Veil or Surge Surfer x0.3, then -10% per Odd Keystone the target's player owns), rounded and stored in sleepCooldown.
effects.resolution: triggerSleep does nothing when the target is already asleep, has Rune Protect, is skydiving, has the IMMUNITY_SLEEP effect, or has ccCooldown above 0. If it applies: sleep = true and sleepCooldown = rounded duration; a Chesto Berry holder eats it right away (eatBerry body not read). While asleep the unit cannot move or attack (COMATOSE passive excepted). Each damage instance it receives (onDamageReceived) shortens the remaining sleep by 300 ms. When the sleep ends, ccCooldown is raised to at least 1500 ms (CC_COOLDOWN), which blocks a new sleep (and other crowd control) during that window.

statusEffects.duration: requested 2000 ms (4000 fallback) x (1 + AP/100) x crit; applied after weather, rage and duration reductions

starBehavior.note: Caster stars choose the number of targets (1, 2, 3; fallback 5) and the base duration (2000 ms for stars 1 to 3, 4000 ms fallback). Catalog units here are 1 (IGGLYBUFF), 2 (JIGGLYPUFF) and 3 (WIGGLYTUFF) stars, so every catalog caster has a 2000 ms base.

record.positionalConditions: No range or area limit; ordering uses positionY only. Fewer enemies than N on the board means only the available ones are slept (rank[i] undefined is skipped).
record.repeatedCastsAndModes: No stored state. A repeat cast can re-pick the same enemies, but triggerSleep refuses a unit that is already asleep or still inside the ccCooldown window after waking.
record.rawVsResolved: Requested: 2000 ms base (stars 1-3) scaled by AP and crit, on 1 / 2 / 3 enemies. Applied: only on enemies that pass the triggerSleep guards (not asleep, no Rune Protect, not skydiving, no sleep immunity, ccCooldown 0); duration then changed by weather, rage and the status-duration reductions, and shortened by 300 ms per damage instance. A ranked enemy that is refused still counts toward N (the loop does not skip to the next enemy).
